## Creating it

Factory functions (the usual way - every element is held in a `std::shared_ptr`):

```cpp
std::shared_ptr<UltraCanvasBarChartElement> CreateBarChartElement( const std::string &id, int x, int y, int width, int height);   // Bar Chart Factory
```

Constructors:

```cpp
UltraCanvasBarChartElement(const std::string &id, int x, int y, int width, int height);
```

The first string argument is always the element's **identifier**, never its text (see [Core concepts](../Core-Concepts.md#identifiers)).

Hooks for a class that derives from this one.

| `CalculateDataBounds` | `ChartDataBounds CalculateDataBounds() override` | The value axis always includes 0, so bars rise from (or hang below) the zero line; it is padded only away from zero and then rounded out to the next whole tick. A value range replaces it. |
| `CalculatePlotArea` | `ChartPlotArea CalculatePlotArea() override` | Horizontal bars need room on the left for the category names. |
| `RenderGrid` | `void RenderGrid(IRenderContext *ctx) override` | Grid lines on the value ticks only: lines across the categories would run through the bars. |

| `GetYAxisTickTarget` | `int GetYAxisTickTarget() const override` | Eight: the axis is rounded out to a whole tick, and the finer the step the less room that rounding leaves empty. |

## Option types in this header

### enum `BarChartOrientation`

Which way the bars run. Vertical: categories along the bottom, values up the left. Horizontal: one row per category, its name on the left, values along the bottom - the form for "power by device" or any list of named amounts whose names are longer than a bar is wide.
